claims.evidence: Witness report shows motorcycle engine assemblies in a workshop; no origin paperwork, labels, or import markings are shown.
Witness report shows exposed engine components; no running/test video, sound recording, or test result is shown.
Witness report includes no odometer/ECU reading or service history.
Witness report notes some units appear partially disassembled; no seal/fastener evidence is provided to confirm never opened.

claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts.
claims.evidence: Witness report only covers motorcycle engine assemblies; it does not confirm the seller’s business scope.

risks.risk: Engine may be incomplete or missing key parts (wiring, sensors, carb/injector, starter/alternator, covers), which affects whether it can be installed and run.
risks.proof: A full set of clear photos showing the complete engine assembly from all sides including: carb/injector, intake/exhaust, starter/alternator, wiring harness/connectors, and all covers/fasteners; plus a short clip of the engine being started.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a partially disassembled/unknown-completeness engine assembly (spares value), not a guaranteed running unit.

risks.risk: Condition may be poor despite claims (internal wear, compression loss, leaks, bent shafts, cracked cylinder head/block).
risks.proof: Compression test reading (video/photo of gauge results) and leak test/inspection photos of cylinder walls, head surface, and any cracks; plus a running clip showing stable idle.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst-case for used engines: not confirmed working; treat as for parts/repair.

risks.risk: “No knock” claim cannot be verified; knocking could appear only under load or after warm-up.
risks.proof: Start-and-run video (cold start if possible) with clear audio for 30–60 seconds, ideally under light load.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially noisy/needs overhaul until proven otherwise.

risks.risk: Wrong fitment risk: exact make/model/year compatibility is unknown, so buyer may not be able to use it for their bike.
risks.proof: Photos of engine ID/part numbers (stamped numbers on block/head) and the exact motorcycle make/model/year it came from; plus a matching parts list from the seller.
risks.if_unproven: Price as unknown-fitment engine assembly; buyer assumes compatibility risk.

risks.risk: Potential scam/overstatement risk: seller claims “tested and working” and “never opened” while witness sees partially disassembled units.
risks.proof: Video proof of testing (start/run) and close-up photos of seals/fasteners to show whether it was opened; also show the full engine as one complete unit.
risks.if_unproven: Price conservatively as unverified condition; do not pay as if it is confirmed running.

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the engine ID/part numbers (block/head) and any label/marking that indicates make/model/year.
Send photos showing the engine is complete: starter/alternator, wiring harness/connectors, carb/injector, intake/exhaust, and all covers.
Send a short start-and-run video with clear audio (cold start preferred) showing stable idle and no abnormal knocking.
Provide compression test results (photo/video of gauge readings) and any leak test/inspection photos.
Show close-ups of cylinder head/block surfaces and any potential cracks, stripped threads, or bent shafts.
response.reason: The witness confirms only that motorcycle engine assemblies are present and some appear partially disassembled; the seller’s key claims (tested/working, no knock, never opened, low mileage) are not verifiable from the report. Without proof of completeness and working condition, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
